plain_question: Can growth happen if power cannot reach the load?
money_path: customer demand -> capital plan -> generation/transmission/distribution work -> regulated recovery or contracted revenue -> operating cash
main_subthemes: data-center demand; grid modernization; regulated recovery; contractor capacity; customer-cash boundary
proof_gap: billing determinants, customer receipts, project-level returns, and financing source/use by project
safe_use: Use as power-as-growth-constraint evidence, not final customer-cash proof.

core_bottleneck: routes from savings and insurance liabilities into assets
plain_question: Who gathers the money and where does it legally go?
money_path: investor or policyholder capital -> fund/account/insurer/BDC/CLO -> borrower/asset/project/security -> fees, interest, spread, repayment, sale proceeds
example_companies: BlackRock; Blackstone; Apollo/Athene; KKR/Global Atlantic; Brookfield
main_subthemes: private credit; insurance balance sheets; fee-bearing AUM; spread income; legal-entity proof gap
proof_gap: receipts, legal-entity schedules, debt waterfalls, collateral files, borrower source/use, and return models
safe_use: Use as capital-routing evidence, not proof that every platform dollar reached a named borrower.

core_bottleneck: equipment, parts, and support needed to keep physical work running
plain_question: Who gets paid when downtime is too costly?
money_path: customer operating need -> rental/parts/service/distribution supplier -> fleet, branch, inventory, technician, or onsite system -> customer uptime -> revenue and cash collection
example_companies: United Rentals; Fastenal; WESCO; Grainger; Applied Industrial
main_subthemes: rental over ownership; MRO distribution; branch density; vendor-managed inventory; cash-conversion risk
proof_gap: inventory turns, receivable collection, customer retention, branch economics, and product/category margins
safe_use: Use as physical-uptime theme evidence; expand distributors before making sector-wide claims.

core_bottleneck: organized access to care under reimbursement and labor pressure
plain_question: Who controls the route from patient need to paid care?
money_path: patient need -> payer/PBM/provider/care-site operator -> authorized service, prescription, dialysis, home visit, or infusion -> premium or reimbursement -> operating cash
example_companies: UnitedHealth; Cigna; DaVita; Addus; Option Care
main_subthemes: payer routing; chronic care; alternate-site care; labor constraint; reimbursement boundary
proof_gap: service-line cash collection, reimbursement durability, labor cost, patient outcome, and quality evidence
safe_use: Use as healthcare-access system evidence, not patient-outcome or care-quality proof.

core_bottleneck: repair and replacement needs in homes, buildings, and civic infrastructure
plain_question: Who gets paid because the physical world wears out?
money_path: owner/contractor/builder/municipality need -> retailer/distributor/manufacturer/branch channel -> product or service input -> upkeep or project completion -> margin and cash
example_companies: Home Depot; Lowe’s; Core & Main; Builders FirstSource; Sherwin-Williams
main_subthemes: repair and maintenance; Pro channel; water infrastructure; surface renewal; working-capital proof
proof_gap: ticket/transaction split, Pro/DIY mix, inventory, receivables, branch economics, municipal funding, and free cash flow
safe_use: Use as upkeep-economy evidence while preserving company-specific cash-quality gaps.

core_bottleneck: security, routing, identity, access, and governance for online systems
plain_question: Who gets paid because digital activity must be controlled?
money_path: digital activity -> need for speed/security/policy/governance -> control-layer provider -> subscription, usage, hardware/software, or platform fee -> revenue, billings, RPO, FCF
main_subthemes: access policy; edge routing; security enforcement; platform governance; operating leverage boundary
proof_gap: gross retention, net retention, usage margin, contract durability, safety cost, and free-cash-flow conversion
safe_use: Use as digital-control evidence, not proof every platform has durable operating leverage.

plain_question: Where does money go when households need their paychecks to stretch?
money_path: household pressure -> shopping-trip choice -> retailer format/membership/private label/off-price/essential basket -> traffic, basket, margin, membership or ad revenue -> cash
example_companies: Costco; Walmart; Target; Dollar General; Burlington
main_subthemes: membership value; trade-down; off-price discovery; essentials vs discretionary; inventory quality
proof_gap: traffic/ticket split, shrink, inventory markdowns, fulfillment costs, membership renewal, and operating-cash-flow quality
safe_use: Use as pressured-consumer evidence while separating each retailer format.

core_bottleneck: time, experience, convenience, status, and routine
plain_question: What do people keep paying for beyond physical goods?
money_path: consumer desire -> hotel/platform/restaurant/venue/casino/loyalty system -> stay, meal, trip, entertainment, or service occasion -> take rate, room revenue, franchise fee, food margin, or gaming revenue
main_subthemes: experience spending; habit loops; loyalty systems; platform take rates; discretionary fragility
proof_gap: company extractions, traffic, occupancy, RevPAR, same-store sales, loyalty economics, and margin/cash conversion
safe_use: Use as a writing candidate until company extraction is completed.

core_bottleneck: trusted routines, brands, taste, family identity, and self-presentation
plain_question: Why do small repeat purchases carry pricing power?
money_path: household routine or identity need -> brand manufacturer -> retailer/distributor/direct route -> product purchase -> price/mix, volume, margin, repeat purchase, and cash
example_companies: P&G; Colgate; Estee Lauder; Coca-Cola; Hasbro
main_subthemes: trusted routine; brand price power; beauty/status; child/family culture; volume boundary
proof_gap: company extractions, price/volume split, organic volume, gross margin, promotion, retailer power, and cash conversion
safe_use: Use as a brand-and-routine candidate; do not infer durable volume until extracted.

core_bottleneck: physical inputs needed for construction, electrification, agriculture, and industry
plain_question: What happens when growth needs scarce inputs?
money_path: end-market demand -> mine/mill/plant/quarry/fertilizer producer -> physical input sold -> realized price, shipment volume, margin, and cash
example_companies: Freeport-McMoRan; Nucor; Steel Dynamics; Vulcan; CF Industries
main_subthemes: copper constraint; steel cycle; aggregates scarcity; fertilizer/food; commodity boundary
proof_gap: non-STLD extractions, shipment/mix, realized price, cost curve, end-market linkage, and through-cycle cash
safe_use: Use as physical-input evidence while separating commodity price from durable cash quality.

core_bottleneck: sites that cannot easily be replicated
plain_question: Where does location become a control point?
money_path: tenant/user demand -> tower/warehouse/data-center/medical/retail/housing site -> lease, rent, occupancy, renewal, escalation, or service payment -> property cash flow
example_companies: American Tower; Prologis; Equinix; Welltower; Realty Income
main_subthemes: network sites; logistics location; care location; triple-net durability; rate boundary
proof_gap: company extractions, occupancy, rent growth, renewals, tenant health, debt cost, cap rates, and AFFO quality
safe_use: Use as a location-scarcity candidate until property-level evidence is extracted.

core_bottleneck: compute, chips, networks, enterprise workflows, and automation infrastructure
plain_question: What tech matters when software needs physical and enterprise infrastructure?
money_path: enterprise/cloud/developer need -> chip/hardware/software/network/workflow provider -> license, subscription, device, cloud, support, or usage revenue -> margin, backlog, deferred revenue, and cash
main_subthemes: compute scarcity; enterprise workflow; hardware-software bundles; infrastructure lock-in; capex boundary
proof_gap: company extractions, AI customer ROI, backlog durability, gross margin, capex intensity, and free cash flow
safe_use: Use as a broad-tech candidate; avoid treating AI demand as final customer-return proof.

core_bottleneck: devices, diagnostics, distribution, hospital capacity, and clinical infrastructure
plain_question: What hidden systems make care possible?
money_path: provider/lab/hospital/patient need -> device/diagnostics/distribution/hospital/tools company -> procedure, test, drug delivery, stay, equipment, consumable, or service -> revenue, margin, reimbursement, and cash
example_companies: Abbott; Thermo Fisher; HCA; McKesson; Stryker
main_subthemes: procedure volume; diagnostics/labs; drug distribution; hospital capacity; reimbursement boundary
proof_gap: company extractions, procedure volume, payer mix, working capital, reimbursement, inventory, and outcome boundaries
safe_use: Use as a medical-infrastructure candidate until company proof packets exist.

core_bottleneck: physical route from resource to user
plain_question: Can energy reach the buyer at an affordable price?
money_path: resource/customer demand -> producer/pipeline/processor/exporter/refiner -> movement, processing, liquefaction, sale, tariff, fee, or spread -> EBITDA, DCF, OCF, dividends, debt repayment, or reinvestment
example_companies: Exxon; Energy Transfer; ONEOK; Plains; Cheniere
main_subthemes: route control; export optionality; fee vs commodity exposure; capital intensity; contract boundary
proof_gap: shipper identity, tariff billing, committed volume, asset-level contribution, and project return
safe_use: Use as supply-route evidence, not final asset-level return proof.

core_bottleneck: daily rails for spending, saving, borrowing, insuring, paying, and settling
plain_question: What do deposits, cards, claims, loans, and payment fees reveal about stress?
money_path: household/business transaction -> bank/card issuer/insurer/payment network/lender -> deposit, loan, premium, claim, fee, interest, provision, or network fee -> earnings, losses, capital, and cash
example_companies: JPMorgan; American Express; Capital One; Progressive; Visa
main_subthemes: deposit cost; card spending; credit losses; insurance pricing; payment rails
proof_gap: Progressive and Visa extraction, loss-adjusted profitability, delinquencies, charge-offs, claims, combined ratio, and payment-volume economics
safe_use: Use as ordinary-money-system evidence after finishing Progressive and Visa.
